AUTHOR: Konovalov
TITLE: Underwater fish detection with weak multi-domain supervision
REGION: Palm Islands, Great Barrier Reef, Queensland, Australia
SPECIES: fish/no-fish binary (juvenile reef/mangrove fish, e.g., Lutjanus argentimaculatus, Caranx sexfasciatus)
DATA: Own unbaited RUV clips from 20 habitats (FD10 / FD10-Test); weak supervision from VOC2012 (negatives), LCF-15 and QUT2014 (positives)
V_EV: Sec. II.A: 'levels of suspended sediments, organic flocculation (marine snow), turbidity and salinity.' (sites varied; not measured)
D2: every 10th frame of each clip to training (FD10, 80/20 train/val random), remaining frames of same clips to test (FD10-Test)
D_EV: Sec. III.A: 'Since every 10th frame was used for training (or validation), it was reasonable to expect that the remaining test frames ... would be classified exactly'
R_EV: Sec. III.A: 'All FD10 and FD10c trained models (Table I) were applied to the FD10-Test dataset'
C_EV: Sec. III.A: 'The default 0.5 threshold was used to accept the CNN activation output as positive/fish'
E_EV: Table I: 'CONFUSION MATRIX FOR THE FD10-TEST DATASET' (FP/N, FN/P, AUC only)
ARCH: Xception-based binary classifier (XFishMp, XFishHmMp heatmap variant); weak multi-domain supervision
METR: FP rate, FN rate, ROC AUC, confusion matrix
NOTE: Train/test frames interleaved from the same clips (systematic every-10th-frame, not random but frame-level); authors explicitly note test frames should be classified almost exactly because of this -> D4=Y, D_ALL=P (verifier may judge that remark insufficient as leakage discussion -> D_ALL=N). External datasets used only for training. C_ALL gap: default 0.5 threshold used as-is, FP/FN rates and AUC reported (FP discussion exists, so N rule not strictly met, but no threshold sensitivity analysis so P not met) -> coded N as lower-information value. Turbidity/sediment variation mentioned qualitatively. 600 project videos mentioned but number of training clips not reported. NIMG = 'In total the clips yielded 40,000 frames'.
